MSU research activities focused on the initial aspects of fabricating suitable membrane materials (ceramics, metals, and polymers) and demonstrating the potential for both axial and transverse gradients in cast and sintered tapes through the development of a new slurry delivery system. Further activities focused on integrating membranes with OCOchem testing systems to evaluate the influence of the FTC membranes on existing 9 cm2 and 100 cm2 systems and to demonstrate scale up to and beyond 300 cm2. Given that FTC methods are generally performed from 10 - 40 vol% solids loading, a system was designed and built with syringe pumps, static mixing nozzles, and an Arduino-controlled slurry metering system to continuously change solids loading as the tape is cast. Given that porosity is generated from water content and the solidification of water to ice, followed by sublimation, the metering process simply needed to match to the casting rate to achieve lateral gradients, as depicted in Figure 6.
